name: Patchwork Collective Scrap Tee
description:
There is no single Patchwork Collective Scrap Tee — each one is unique. They're assembled by the loose network of Shelf sewers and textile scavengers who trade under the Patchwork Collective name, stitching together salvaged fabric scraps, old band shirts, industrial textile remnants, and whatever else is available into something wearable. The base structure is usually a simple crew-neck tee shape, but the surface is a map of wherever the fabric came from — a stripe of Ghanaian kente-print synth cotton next to a panel of faded logistics-corp khaki next to a scrap of what might have been a child's blanket.

They're sold at Shelf markets, traded between residents, and occasionally show up in Tier 2 neighborhoods where people buy them as art objects. On the Shelf, they're just clothes — warm enough, structurally sound, repaired and re-repaired. The stitching is sometimes crude and sometimes extraordinarily fine, depending on who made it. No two are the same.
what_it_says: You make do. You make it work. You might also be making a point.
worn_by: Tier 2 people who grew up on the Shelf
people who buy things with histories
story_hooks: A specific scrap tee contains a fragment of fabric from a garment worn during the 2171 Shelf uprising — and someone recognizes it.
The Patchwork Collective has started embedding small, coded messages in the stitching patterns — a communication network hiding in plain sight.
A Tier 5 fashion house has begun producing 'authentic' Patchwork Collective-inspired pieces for Φ1,200. The Collective has opinions about this.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deconstructed crew-neck tee that reads as a textile collage — a patchwork map of salvaged materials creating an intentionally chaotic, layered visual. Each garment is visually unique, combining geometric fabric scraps in jarring adjacency. The overall silhouette is a simple, relaxed tee, but the surface tells a story of scarcity and resourcefulness.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, slightly oversized through the torso. Comfortable for movement and layering. Sleeves are standard length, cut with variable precision depending on maker skill.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged mixed textiles — synth-cotton, industrial khaki weave, kente-print synthetics, reclaimed blanket fleece, repurposed band-shirt cotton, logistics-grade polyester blends. No two sections match.
physical_description.texture: Highly varied — smooth sections adjacent to rough industrial weave, soft printed cotton next to stiff logistics fabric. Surface is tactilely chaotic. Stitching is visible and integral to the aesthetic, ranging from crude hand-stitched seams to precise machine work.
physical_description.color_scheme: No unified palette. Typical combinations include faded khaki corporate branding, vibrant kente geometric patterns, aged band-shirt graphics, muted fleece tones, and worn denim blues. Colors clash intentionally.
physical_description.closures: None — simple crew neck, no collar, standard short sleeves.
distinctive_features: Each piece is one-of-one — no two exist identically
Visible patchwork seams are design elements, not flaws
May include faded corporate logos, band graphics, or textile mill stamps
Evidence of previous repairs and re-stitching visible
Often shows patina of multiple previous owners
Some sections may be intentionally distressed; others pristine
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 origin, Tier 3 street adoption, Tier 2 collectible. Signals different things depending on context — on the Shelf, it's functional necessity; in wealthy neighborhoods, it's commodified authenticity.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this declares connection to Shelf economies, DIY textile culture, and post-scarcity fashion sensibility. It's a statement against new manufacturing and corporate clothing uniformity. Worn by scavengers, Shelf dwellers, and wealthy people performing sustainability.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn-in and lived-in. Visible mending, faded patches, soft from repeated washing. May show stains, careful repairs, or reinforced seams where previous owners extended garment life. Authenticity comes from wear.
